title: What to do in a heatwave: BMC do's and don'ts
summary: BMC's official heatwave guidance for residents, including how to help someone with sunstroke.
details: Avoid going out in the sun, especially between 12 noon and 3 pm.
Drink water often even if not thirsty; use ORS, lassi, buttermilk, lemon water or torani.
Avoid alcohol, tea, coffee and carbonated soft drinks, which dehydrate the body.
Keep your home cool with curtains or shutters and open windows at night.
For sunstroke: lay the person in shade, wipe with a wet cloth, give ORS and take them to the nearest health centre.

sources.title: BMC Disaster Management: Do's and Don'ts (Heatwave)

title: Check IMD heat and weather warnings for Greater Mumbai
summary: IMD's urban weather page for Greater Mumbai gives station observations, heatwave monitoring, nowcasts and district warnings.
details: Shows current readings for Mumbai City, Santacruz and suburban stations.
Includes heatwave/coldwave forecasts, district-wise warnings and thunderstorm nowcasts.
Use it before planning outdoor work or travel on hot or stormy days.

sources.title: India Meteorological Department: Urban Meteorology, Greater Mumbai

title: See the live heat index at your nearest BMC weather station
summary: BMC's Disaster Management portal shows 15-minute readings, including heat index and rainfall, for a station you pick.
details: Select your area under Weather Updates to see temperature, humidity, heat index and rainfall.
Readings are the last 15 minutes of data from BMC weather stations.
The same page shows IMD's 24- and 48-hour forecast for the city and suburbs.

title: Call 108 for a free ambulance in a heatstroke emergency
summary: Maharashtra Emergency Medical Services runs a free, 24x7 ambulance service on 108.
details: Dial 108 (toll-free) from any phone.
The service is free of cost to patients and runs 24x7.
Aims to reach the nearest hospital within the 'golden hour'.

sources.title: Maharashtra Public Health Department: Maharashtra Emergency Medical Services (MEMS)

title: Check hourly air quality (AQI) on the Sameer app
summary: The Central Pollution Control Board's Sameer app gives hourly National AQI readings and lets you file air pollution complaints.
details: Free on Android; published by the Central Pollution Control Board.
Shows hourly National Air Quality Index with colour codes.
Lets you register and track air pollution complaints.

sources.title: Google Play: Sameer (Central Pollution Control Board)

title: Report construction dust or garbage burning to BMC
summary: BMC's air pollution rules require dust controls on building sites and ban open burning; you can report breaches through BMC's complaint channels.
details: Rules: sites over 1 acre need barricades at least 35 ft high (25 ft under 1 acre), plus water fogging and tyre washing at exits.
Open burning is completely banned anywhere in BMC limits.
Report on 1916 (24x7), the MyBMC app, or WhatsApp +91 8999228999.
Online complaints and status tracking: marg.mcgm.gov.in.

sources.title: BMC: Guidelines for Air Pollution Mitigation (25.10.2023)

title: Rooftop solar subsidy for your home (PM Surya Ghar)
summary: A central government subsidy for households that install rooftop solar; apply online with your electricity account number.
details: Subsidy: Rs 30,000 per kW up to 2 kW, Rs 18,000 per kW for additional capacity up to 3 kW, capped at Rs 78,000.
Suggested size: 1–2 kW for 0–150 units a month, 2–3 kW for 150–300 units.
Apply at pmsuryaghar.gov.in with your mobile number, then pick your state, district, utility and consumer number.
The portal says the scheme closes on 31 March 2027.

sources.title: MNRE: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana national portal

title: Rooftop solar subsidy for housing societies (PM Surya Ghar)
summary: Group housing societies and RWAs can claim a subsidy for solar that powers common areas, including EV charging.
details: Rs 18,000 per kW for common facilities, including EV charging.
Up to 500 kW per society, at 3 kW per house, including residents' own rooftop plants.
Apply on the same national portal before the 31 March 2027 closing date.

sources.title: MNRE: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana national portal

title: Switch to Adani Electricity's green tariff
summary: Adani Electricity consumers in the suburbs can opt to have their supply matched with renewable power for a small extra charge.
details: Extra charge: Rs 0.25 per unit, as stated on the page.
Opt in through 'Switch To Green' on the green tariff page.
A green certificate is issued to participating consumers.
Customer care: 19122 (toll-free, 24x7).

title: Apply for rooftop solar net metering with BEST
summary: BEST electricity consumers in the island city can connect a rooftop solar system and get credit for power exported to the grid.
details: Apply online with system details; BEST acknowledges within 3 working days.
Technical feasibility within 15 working days; approval within 7 working days, valid for 6 months.
After installation, BEST tests and commissions within 10 working days, then you sign the net metering agreement.

title: Report waterlogging, fallen trees or blocked drains on 1916
summary: BMC's 24x7 central helpline takes civic and disaster complaints, including flooding and drainage.
details: WhatsApp: +91 8999228999 (MyBMC Assist).
Or file online at marg.mcgm.gov.in and track status with your complaint number.

sources.title: BMC Disaster Management: Central Complaint Registration System

title: Get flood and rain alerts on the Disaster Management BMC app
summary: BMC's official app gives 15-minute rainfall and weather readings, tide times, IMD nowcast warnings and nearby shelters.
details: Free on Android, published by Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation.
Data from 60+ automatic weather stations, updated every 15 minutes.
Shows tides, traffic and transit status, IMD nowcasts, and nearby police stations, hospitals, shelters and flood-prone areas.
Has an SOS button for emergency contacts.

title: What to do before, during and after urban flooding
summary: BMC's official checklist for Mumbai's monsoon flooding.
details: Stay home if heavy rain and high tide coincide.
Keep a torch, food, drinking water, dry clothes and documents ready; move valuables higher.
Switch off electricity and gas at the mains; don't walk or drive through flowing water.
Afterwards, drink only boiled or chlorinated water and don't eat food that touched floodwater.

sources.title: BMC Disaster Management: Do's and Don'ts (Urban Floods)

title: BMC Flood Preparedness Guidelines 2026: your ward's flood plan and contacts
summary: BMC's 319-page monsoon handbook for 2026, with ward-by-ward contacts, flood-vulnerable areas and high-tide days.
details: Section II is a directory for every ward (from page 95), so you can find your ward office's contacts.
Includes each ward's action plan, flood vulnerability and the year's high-tide and neap-tide days.
Section III covers the fire brigade, beach safety, fallen trees and branches, public health and traffic police.
Open the embedded PDF on the page; it is large, so it may take a minute to load on mobile data.

sources.title: BMC Disaster Management: Flood Preparedness Guidelines 2026

title: Buy metro, bus and train tickets in one app (Mumbai One)
summary: The official Mumbai One app plans trips and sells QR tickets across metro, bus and suburban routes.
details: Published by Maha Mumbai Metro Operation Corporation Ltd (MMMOCL).
QR tickets for contactless travel, including return tickets on Metro Lines 1 and 3.
Compares routes across operators to find the fastest or cheapest option.

title: Maharashtra EV Policy 2025: tax waiver and purchase incentive
summary: Electric vehicles registered in Maharashtra until March 2030 pay no motor vehicle tax, and eligible models get a purchase incentive.
details: 100% motor vehicle tax exemption and registration fee waiver for EVs registered during the policy period.
E-two-wheelers: 10% of ex-factory cost, up to Rs 10,000 (first 1,00,000 vehicles).
Private e-cars: 10% of ex-factory cost, up to Rs 1,50,000 (first 10,000 vehicles).
No tolls for passenger EVs on the Mumbai–Pune Expressway, Samruddhi Mahamarg and Atal Setu.
Policy period: 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2030.

sources.title: Maharashtra Transport Department: EV Policy 2025 GR (23.05.2025)

title: Book free debris pickup after home repairs
summary: BMC collects construction and demolition waste from your door; small loads are free.
details: Up to 500 kg: free transport and processing.
Book on the BMC C&D waste app or by phone.
City and Eastern Suburbs: 1800-202-6364. Western Suburbs: 1800-210-9976.
Above 500 kg, charges apply under the C&D Waste Management Policy 2025.

title: Find an authorised e-waste recycler in Mumbai
summary: MPCB publishes the list of authorised e-waste recyclers, dismantlers and refurbishers, including several in Mumbai.
details: The March 2024 list includes Mumbai recyclers, for example in Sakinaka and Kurla.
Hand old phones, laptops and appliances only to units on the authorised list.
MPCB's e-waste page also links the state authorisation registry.

sources.title: MPCB: Authorised e-waste recyclers and refurbishers (March 2024)

title: Report single-use plastic being sold or used
summary: Maharashtra bans many single-use plastic and thermocol items; MPCB runs a helpline for the ban.
details: The ban comes under the Maharashtra Plastic and Thermocol Products Notification, 2018 (amended up to 30 November 2022).
MPCB single-use plastic ban helpline: (022) 24010437 or (022) 24020781 extension 323.
